what: independent re-scoring of full32_dolmino@step25000 on the two RATIO-flip-critical axes (nq_open, popqa) plus triviaqa, protocol-identical to the 2026-08-03 archive, to settle whether A04's first non-trivial rule disagreement survives

protocol_recovered.source: logs/cb_full32_step25000_sched.out and logs/cb_full32_step25000_nqopen_sched.out on zwfy6 -- the archive's OWN scheduler logs, which echo the full parameter set
protocol_recovered.task_split: popqa,triviaqa in one invocation then nq_open in a second -- matching the archive's two-call structure
protocol_recovered.scorer_unchanged_since: commit 9fabb88 (2026-08-02), i.e. before the 2026-08-03 archive -- so this is a same-CODE comparison, not a code-version diff

integrity.loader: proposal/shared/code/canonical_eval_loaders.py::load_cb -- enforces 8/8 shards, exact n, no duplicate item_id, no nan; merge NOT hand-rolled
integrity.shards: 8/8 on every axis, shard_fail=0 on both merges

result.headline: BIT-IDENTICAL. All three re-scored axes reproduce the archive to the last digit, with ZERO item flips and ZERO prediction-string flips; 24/24 per-example shard files are byte-identical (sha256).

sensitivity_batch_size_probe.why: a same-protocol re-run is bit-identical, so it bounds RUNTIME jitter at exactly 0.0 pp but says nothing about how fragile RATIO is to a perturbation that DOES move items. Batch size is the known such perturbation on this harness (bf16 numerics depend on left-pad width). bs=48 vs the archive's 32 is therefore the informative probe.
sensitivity_batch_size_probe.admissibility: NOT an admissible re-measurement -- the frozen protocol is bs=32. These numbers quantify fragility; they never enter a verdict.
sensitivity_batch_size_probe.finding: under a genuine item-moving perturbation (22 items flipped across the two axes) RATIO's margin WIDENS from +0.0014951 to +0.0020291 -- it does not approach the flip point. The two flip-critical axes moved in OPPOSITE directions (popqa -0.014 pp, nq_open +0.055 pp), which is why the mean is more stable than any single axis.
